@graph.headline: Home Builder Market Research: A Practical Framework
@graph.description: Use a practical home builder market research framework to define geography, demand, audience, competitors, proof, sources, limits, decisions, and review dates.

mainEntity.name: What is home builder market research?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a decision-focused process that combines official market data, business evidence, customer research, search behavior, and current competitor information within stated boundaries and limitations.

mainEntity.name: Which sources are useful for builder market research?

acceptedAnswer.text: Useful sources include Census and HUD housing data, building permits, ACS estimates, business and sales records, approved interviews, validated analytics, and current public competitor pages.

mainEntity.name: Can national housing data predict local builder demand?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. National and regional data can provide context, but local demand and business fit require appropriately scoped evidence, operational review, and direct testing.

mainEntity.name: How should competitor research be used?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use public competitor pages to understand visible positioning, services, markets, proof, and content gaps. Do not treat those claims as verified performance or copy their language.
It is complete enough for a decision when the question, boundaries, sources, limits, owner, next test, metric, and stop condition are documented. It should still receive a review date.
